guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case for Purdue starts with quarterback continuity rather than its opening result. Ryan Browne started every game last season, then completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards and three touchdowns against Indiana State. That performance is encouraging context, but our longer-run efficiency numbers remain skeptical of Purdue’s passing attack, especially against a UCLA pass defense that grades as the stronger unit in that matchup.

The bigger concern for us is whether Purdue can consistently keep UCLA out of favorable scoring situations. Our numbers give UCLA meaningful advantages on the ground and in creating scoring opportunities. Purdue held Indiana State to 66 rushing yards, but one result does not erase that broader concern, particularly for a roster that had 16 players make their first Purdue starts in the opener. The market is asking UCLA to turn those advantages into substantial separation; our model is less convinced, but the disagreement is not large enough for us to play Purdue at the current price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching UCLA’s rushing offense against Purdue’s front. If UCLA can run efficiently and repeatedly reach scoring range, it has the clearest path to creating the margin the market expects. Purdue’s opener offered some positive evidence—66 rushing yards allowed, with three sacks and eight tackles for loss—but we need more than one game before treating that defensive performance as a new baseline.

recent_game.fact: Purdue opened the 2026 season with a 44-19 home victory over Indiana State on Sept. 4.
Purdue produced 523 yards of total offense against Indiana State, its first 500-yard game since Oct. 12, 2024 at Illinois.
Purdue had no turnovers and won the turnover battle against Indiana State.
Sixteen players made their first starts as Boilermakers and 38 players made their Purdue debuts in the season opener.

opponent_notes.fact: Purdue is scheduled to play UCLA at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena on Sept. 19, 2026, with an 11 p.m. ET kickoff on BTN.
The 11 p.m. ET kickoff against UCLA would be Purdue's latest start since an 11:05 p.m. ET game at Hawaii on Nov. 25, 2006.
The UCLA game will be Purdue's third game at the Rose Bowl venue and its first there outside the Rose Bowl Game.
Barry Odom has not previously faced UCLA as a head coach.

quarterback.fact: Starting quarterback Ryan Browne completed 23 of 29 passes for 317 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions against Indiana State.
Browne's season opener was his fourth career 300-yard passing game and his 15th career start for Purdue.
Browne started all 12 games in 2025 and threw for 2,153 yards with nine touchdowns.
Browne returned to Purdue during the spring transfer window in 2025 after spending the spring semester at North Carolina.
Evans Chuba and Bennett Meredith competed for the backup quarterback position during the spring and summer.

offensive_personnel.fact: Minnesota transfer Fame Ijeboi led Purdue with 87 rushing yards and one touchdown on 11 carries against Indiana State and added two receptions for 30 yards.
FAU transfer Asaad Waseem caught six passes for 107 yards and one touchdown in his Purdue debut.
Iowa State transfer Xavier Townsend caught seven passes for 47 yards and returned three punts for 24 yards in his Purdue debut.
Travis Terrell Jr., a transfer from Jackson State, rushed 11 times for 32 yards in his Purdue debut.
George Burhenn caught two passes for 43 yards against Indiana State in his first game action in 349 days.
True freshman Brock Brownfield became Purdue's first true freshman offensive lineman to start a season opener since freshmen became eligible in 1972.
Joey Tanona was the only returning Purdue offensive lineman who started all 12 games in 2025; Ethan Trent made six starts and Jude McCoskey played in 11 games.
Purdue added offensive-line transfers Boaz Stanley, Nuku Mafi and Micah Banuelos, who entered the season with 21, 12 and five career starts, respectively.
The running back room lost Devin Mockobee to graduation, with Antonio Harris the only returning running back from 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: FIU transfer Mister Clark recorded five solo tackles, two tackles for loss, one sack and one pass breakup against Indiana State.
Don Saunders returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown against Indiana State, Purdue's first pick-six since 2022.
Linebacker Charles Correa returned after starting all 12 games in 2025 and recording 96 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss and three sacks.
Illinois transfer Jojo Hayden made four tackles, including one tackle for loss, in his Purdue debut against Indiana State.
Defensive lineman Ian Jeffries recorded three tackles and one sack against Indiana State.
Purdue added defensive linemen Rodney Lora, Curt Neal and Wisdom Simms, who brought a combined 81 games of college experience, including 60 at the Power Four level.
The defensive backfield added transfers Jaden Mangham, Don Saunders, John Slaughter and Justin Denson Jr.; Mangham, Saunders and Slaughter started against Indiana State.

coaching_changes.fact: Kevin Kane returned to Purdue as defensive coordinator and linebackers coach after serving as a Minnesota defensive analyst in 2025; he previously coordinated Purdue's defense in 2023 and 2024.
Zach Crabtree became Purdue's offensive line coach after coaching at Fresno State in 2025 and previously working with offensive coordinator Josh Henson at USC.
Cornell Ford moved from wide receivers coach to running backs coach for 2026.
Bilal Marshall was promoted from offensive analyst to wide receivers coach during the offseason.
Charles Clark joined Purdue as defensive pass game coordinator and defensive backs coach after five seasons at Memphis.

injury_availability.fact: Tight end Kylan Fox suffered an injury at the start of training camp and is expected to miss the 2026 season.
Wide receivers De'Nylon Morrissette and Chauncey Magwood returned for 2026 after missing the 2025 season with injuries.
Magwood played against Indiana State and caught a six-yard touchdown, his first touchdown since 2022.
George Burhenn returned to action against Indiana State after an injury at Notre Dame ended his 2025 season.

offensive_context.fact: Purdue passed for 346 yards and rushed for 177 yards while totaling 523 yards against Indiana State.
Five different players scored Purdue's five touchdowns against Indiana State, and each recorded his first points as a Boilermaker.
Purdue added 32 transfers and 22 freshmen during the 2026 offseason, including 19 transfers from Power Four programs.

defensive_context.fact: Purdue allowed Indiana State 284 total yards and 12 first downs.
Purdue recorded three sacks and eight tackles for loss against Indiana State.
Purdue held Indiana State to 66 rushing yards.

special_teams.fact: True freshman kicker Jacobo Echeverria Lozano made all three field-goal attempts, with a long of 39 yards, and all five extra points against Indiana State.
Echeverria Lozano's three field goals were the most by a Purdue freshman in a game since at least 1995.
Buffalo transfer Dylan Drennan had one 54-yard punt with a 49-yard net in his Purdue debut.
Travis Terrell Jr. entered Purdue after averaging 30 yards per kickoff return with two return touchdowns at Jackson State in 2024.

series_context.fact: Purdue is 0-3-2 all-time against UCLA, and UCLA has won the last two meetings.
Purdue's two previous West Coast games against UCLA resulted in a 0-0 tie in 1959 and a 31-21 loss in 1979; both were played at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum.

other_relevant.fact: The trip to Pasadena is listed as 2,086 miles from Ross-Ade Stadium.
Ryan Browne, Charles Correa, Hudauri Hines, Jude McCoskey, De'Nylon Morrissette and Curt Neal were named Purdue's 2026 team captains.
